rationale:
Evidence: all 60 development trials across iterations 1 to 3 ended off_track with zero finishes. Iteration 2 (kp 1.5, kd 0.5, sensors at y=0.05 spanning +/-0.024 m) is the best so far at 64.09. Iteration 3 moved the sensors forward to y=0.07, widened them to +/-0.03 m, and cut kp, kd and base_speed. It scored lower (61.07), so moving the sensors forward is not the fix. Max_error stays at 0.063 to 0.067 against the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit (body_width/4 cannot raise it above 0.06 within the allowed body range). Steering oscillation is still 0.11 to 0.16 and 1 to 2 line-loss events occur per run, so the loop is still overshooting at the edges of the tape.

Changes from iteration 2, one group at a time: (1) Sensor footprint reduced from 0.012 to 0.008 m. A smaller footprint gives a sharper edge response, so the signal changes less smoothly near the tape boundary. (2) Sensor spread widened to x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03 m at the iteration-2 forward position y=0.05, so the outer sensors keep the tape in view on tight bends and line loss is less likely. (3) kd raised from 0.5 to 0.6 to damp the faster signal change that the finer sensors produce. (4) kp kept at 1.5 and ki at 0.05, since iteration 2 showed kp 1.5 is better than 3.0. (5) base_speed reduced from 1.5 to 1.4, a small margin so the robot can correct at bends. Wheel geometry, mass and body are unchanged to keep the comparison with iteration 2 clean.

Expected result: max_error just under 0.06, steering oscillation below 0.12, and line-loss events at 0 to 1 per run. Progress should rise above 0.2, with a first chance at completion on the oval and s-bend. The slalom may remain the hardest track. The next telemetry should show whether the narrower sensors and wider spread reduced max_error and line loss at this speed.
